newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares slip as Wall St goes into reverse.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares slip as Wall St goes into reverse.

text.p: European stock markets fell on Wednesday from early highs as U.S. figures again raised the possibility of higher interest rates, only a day after data sending the opposite signal pushed Wall Street sharply higher.
The U.S. economic statistics showed conclusively that a day is a long time on global financial markets.
Data out on Tuesday was weaker than expected, propelling the Dow Jones Industial average up 179 points, its second biggest gain in points terms in history.
But investors seeking clues on whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise interest rates when its policy-making committee meets on May 20 got a different message on Wednesday.
Gross domestic product grew 5.6 percent in the first quarter, compared with an expected 4.1 percent, while the price index rose 2.7 percent against a forecast 2.1 percent.

Signs that the Fed might, after all, have to make a pre-emptive strike against inflation pushed down blue chips prices on Wall Street. After 15 minutes' trade, the Dow was down 14.05 points at 6,947.98.

But the effect was more marked in Europe where markets first followed Wall Street's 2.6 percent surge on Tuesday, had second thoughts over the morning, and fell as the U.S. GDP statistics were released.

London's FTSE 100 leapt to a record 4,466.5 in pre-market trading but slid slowly but surely throughout the morning. The losses accelerated on the GDP data and by mid afternoon, the FTSE was down 16.4 points at 4,416.8.

But with U.S. data giving apparently contradictory messages, economists said the markets would await further U.S. economic reports such as Friday's employment figures for further evidence of the likely scale and timing of an interest rate increase.
Following the drop, British shares generally remained directionless before parliamementary elections on Thursday, likely to produce the first Labour government in 18 years.

"The (U.S.) figures weren't good for the T-bond and hit our market," said one dealer. "There was a little bit of action but now we've gone quiet again. There is lethargy ahead of tomorrow's election."

Germany's DAX index of blue chips rose close to an all-time high in early trade and finished up a sturdy 54.88 points or 1.62 percent at 3,474.98, but only because it records floor trade which closed before the U.S. data.
The IBIS index showed a different picture in later electronic trade. It was up just 2.32 points at 3,428.18 at mid afternoon.
French shares followed a similar trend by giving up early strong gains. The CAC-40 index was up a modest 20.38 points or 0.78 percent at 2,623.24 by mid afternoon.
But shares in chemical and pharmaceuticals group Rhone-Poulenc SA were up 5.22 percent at 197.7 francs after the company reported a 6.5 percent rise in its first quarter net income.
On the foreign exchange market, the dollar rose at the scent of higher U.S. interest rates.
It climbed to 1.7317 marks by mid afternoon, up almost a pfennig from 1.7235 in late European trade on Tuesday. It was at 126.94 yen compared with 126.75 on Tuesday.
"It's a case of stronger numbers, stronger dollar more than anything else now," said Ian Amstad, economist at Bankers Trust in London.
The Bundesbank left its key discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular council meeting on Wednesday, a decision which was in line with market expectations.
STOCKS AT 1345 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 16.4 points or 0.37 percent at 4,416.8.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 20.38 points (0.78 percent) at 2,623.24.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed 54.88 points or 1.62 percent higher at 3,474.98. The IBIS index of electronic trade was later up 2.32 points at 3,428.18.
CURRENCIES AT 1345 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7317 marks against 1.7235 in late European trade on Tuesday. It was at 126.94 yen, slightly lower than 126.75 on Tuesday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the aftrenoon at $340.15 an ounce, down from $340.45 at the morning fix and compared with a close in London on Tuesday at $339.95. Silver was at up five cents at $4.70.
